title: Asana vs Gigxomi for Video Editing Agencies
excerpt: Compare Asana and Gigxomi for video editing agency projects, client conversations, editor assignments, approvals, accounting, and payouts.
seoDescription: Asana vs Gigxomi for video editing agencies: compare client conversations, editor assignments, approvals, accounting, delivery, and payouts.
featuredImageAlt: Asana versus Gigxomi decision guide for video editing agencies
introduction: Asana is a mature general-purpose work management platform; Gigxomi is built around the operating path of a video editing business. The useful question is not which product has more features. It is whether your agency mainly needs configurable project coordination or a connected system spanning enquiries, editors, delivery, accounting, and payouts. This guide separates those jobs without pretending either tool is universally better.
verdict: Choose Asana when your organization coordinates many kinds of cross-functional work and values flexible project views, portfolios, goals, workload, rules, and broad integrations. Choose Gigxomi when video editing is the business itself and you want client conversations, managers, editors, tasks, review, delivery, accounting, and payout visibility in one agency workflow. Some established agencies may use Asana for company-wide planning while using a specialist system for production operations.

sections.heading: Where Asana is stronger
paragraphs: Asana has the advantage when work extends far beyond editing. Marketing campaigns, hiring, finance checklists, product launches, event plans, and executive goals can share one structure. Its project views and portfolio-level reporting help operations leaders compare work across departments without forcing every team into a video-specific model.

Its ecosystem also matters. An organization that already has templates, rules, custom fields, forms, reporting conventions, and trained users may gain more from improving that setup than replacing it. Asana is the safer default when the main requirement is flexible coordination across many business functions.
bullets: Flexible views and reusable project templates
Workload and reporting for broader operations
A large integration and partner ecosystem

sections.heading: Where Gigxomi is more specific
paragraphs: A video editing agency rarely begins with a neat task form. A lead may arrive through WhatsApp or Instagram, a manager qualifies it, an editor receives the production work, a client reviews the result, and the business tracks collection and payout state. Gigxomi is designed around that connected sequence rather than treating each stage as a separately configured project.

That specialization can reduce administration for an owner who currently copies chat context into a task tool, explains the same brief to a manager, checks delivery in another system, and calculates editor payouts elsewhere. The tradeoff is deliberate: Gigxomi is not trying to replace every general-purpose planning use case in a diversified company.

sections.heading: How to test both tools with a real editing job
paragraphs: Use one representative project, not a polished demo. Start with an actual enquiry, collect the brief and source links, assign an editor, request a first cut, consolidate feedback, deliver the approved export, and record what the agency owes or receives. Count manual transfers of information, missing notifications, and the number of places a manager must visit.

In Asana, test whether your custom fields and rules make the handoffs obvious to a new manager. In Gigxomi, confirm the connected inbox behavior, team permissions, review path, and financial states fit your policies. The faster interface is less important than the workflow that survives a busy week.

sections.heading: Migration advice for an Asana agency
paragraphs: Do not move every historical task. Export active clients, open projects, editor ownership, due dates, revision status, and only the reference links needed to finish current work. Keep the Asana export as a dated archive and choose a clear cutover date after which new editing enquiries enter the new system.

Map custom statuses before importing: for example intake, brief confirmed, assigned, editing, internal review, client review, approved, and delivered. Run both systems for a short pilot, but name one source of truth for each live project. Dual entry without ownership creates more risk than either product alone.

sections.heading: Who should choose which
paragraphs: Asana fits agencies that need a flexible company-wide work layer, already depend on its reporting and integrations, or manage editing as only one service among many. Gigxomi fits editing-led businesses that want the commercial conversation and production operation closer together, especially when managers coordinate multiple editors and payout context.

A hybrid can be rational: leadership plans quarterly initiatives in Asana while the editing team runs customer-to-delivery work in Gigxomi. If you choose that model, define the boundary clearly. Do not mirror every editing task in both products; pass only milestones and aggregate status into the company planning layer.

decisionChecklist: Is video editing the core service or one department among many?
Where do client enquiries arrive today?
Do portfolio goals and cross-department reporting outweigh a specialist workflow?
How many manual handoffs occur between chat, task, review, accounting, and payout tools?
Which system can a new manager operate correctly after one week?
What data must remain archived for finance and client history?
